//: There is no TypeScript in this repo and there is not going to be. This file
exists so `tsc --noEmit` can type-check the plain ESM sources through their
JSDoc, which catches the class of mistake tests do not: a typo'd property, a
call with the wrong arity, a value used after a branch that made it null.
`checkJs` without `allowJs` emitting anything is the whole point. If someone
later proposes converting core/ to TypeScript, the blocker is in AGENTS.md:
the vendored copies in skill/scripts/ and mcp/src/ must need no build step,
or `make check-vendor` stops being a byte comparison.
Two deliberate relaxations, both about signal-to-noise rather than rigour:
`noImplicitAny` is off. With it on, every unannotated parameter in the
build scripts is an error — 335 of the 383 total — which buries the dozen
findings that mean something. Annotate a signature when the type carries
information; do not annotate to silence a counter.
Tests are excluded. The tools return discriminated response shapes on
purpose (`found: true` carries fields `found: false` does not), so asserting
on them under strict null checks needs a cast per assertion. Casts that
exist to satisfy the checker teach a reader nothing and would have to be
rewritten every time a response shape moves, which pre-1.0 is often. The
tests run on every commit; that is their check.
